name: Alabama

permitless.notes: Permitless carry since Jan 1, 2023 for anyone 19+ who may legally possess a firearm. Holders of a permit from any state may carry at 18. Text gives 18 as the minimum age for open carry.

honors.notes: Honors any state's handgun license (resident or non-resident), but only while the holder is NOT an Alabama resident. Visitors must follow Alabama law. Text says permit holders from any state may carry at 18.

residentPermit.term: 1 to 5 years (applicant chooses); lifetime permit available
residentPermit.issuedBy: County Sheriff (county of residence)
residentPermit.notes: No training required. Age 18 if service member or honorably discharged veteran. Fee max $25/year; lifetime $300 ($150 if 60+). Decision within 30 days. Permit expires if holder moves to another state.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Text says Alabama does not issue non-resident permits (phrased with a question mark). It notes some sheriffs have issued permits to non-resident military and spouses stationed in AL; check with the local sheriff.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to inform on contact, but if an officer asks whether you have a concealed pistol/firearm on you or in your vehicle, you must say so immediately. At a stop, do not touch a loaded handgun unless the officer tells you to.

vehicle.permitHolder: The text does not give vehicle rules specific to permit holders; the AL permit is defined as a permit to carry a pistol in a vehicle or concealed on the person.
vehicle.noPermit: Anyone 19+ who can legally possess a firearm may carry in a vehicle without a permit. Those 18+ may possess/transport a handgun unloaded and secured in a vehicle. The text does not specify glove box/console/trunk rules.
vehicle.notes: At certain off-limits sites a gun left in the vehicle must be hidden and locked in a compartment/container or the vehicle. Employers must let employees keep a lawful pistol hidden (locked if unattended) in their car.

magazineLimit.notes: The text mentions no state magazine capacity limit.

selfDefenseNotes: Text only lists deadly force statutes (13A-3-1 to 13A-3-31, incl. 13A-3-23 defense of person and 13A-3-25 defense of premises) without describing castle doctrine or duty to retreat.

preemption.notes: The Legislature occupies the entire field of firearm, ammunition and accessory regulation; contrary local rules are void. Affected persons may petition the Attorney General to sue.

schools.notes: Carrying a deadly weapon on K-12 premises (incl. school buses) with intent to do bodily harm is a felony; permit holders are exempt from one subsection. School athletic events off-limits without a permit. Univ. of Alabama claims a campus-wide ban incl. parking.

restAreas.notes: Text says carry is allowed in roadside rest areas.

stateParks.notes: Allowed in state parks and WMAs (handguns only) and state/national forests. Parks on Army Corps of Engineers land are off-limits under federal law. TVA developed recreation areas are off-limits.

pollingPlaces.notes: The text does not address polling places.

airports.notes: Carry allowed in parking lots and outside the secure (TSA) area of the terminal.

bars.notes: Text says carry in restaurants that serve alcohol is allowed (no law against it) unless posted. Bars/bar areas are not separately addressed; source advises avoiding bar areas and drinking.

churches.notes: The text does not address places of worship.

stateBuildings.notes: Prohibited without permission in police/sheriff/highway patrol stations, courthouses and annexes, DA office buildings, buildings during city council/county commission meetings, elected officials' primary offices, and buildings with guards plus security screening.

prohibitedPlaces: Police, sheriff or highway patrol station buildings (without permission)
Prisons, jails, halfway houses, detention and community corrections facilities
Inpatient/custodial psychiatric facilities
Courthouses and courthouse annexes
Buildings housing a District Attorney's office
Buildings where a county commission or city council is meeting
Primary office of any elected official
School/college athletic events (unless permit holder)
Professional athletic events (unless permit holder)
Buildings with continuous guards and security screening (magnetometers, key cards, turnstiles)
Demonstrations in public places, and within 1,000 ft of one after an officer's order
TVA developed recreation areas (day use, campgrounds)
Army Corps of Engineers land (federal law)

noGunSigns.notes: No statute gives signs force of law; if asked to leave private property you must leave or face trespass. Statutory off-limits places must post notices at public entrances.

openCarry.notes: Open carry legal without a permit; text gives minimum age 18. Off-limits places still apply. Brandishing is illegal, but merely carrying a holstered pistol is not disorderly conduct.

notes: Permit recognition does not apply to Alabama residents holding another state's permit.
If asked by police whether you are armed, you must say so immediately; do not touch a loaded handgun during a stop unless directed.
Firearms are banned at public demonstrations, and within 1,000 ft after police order you to leave.
Alabama does not define 'loaded'; source suggests treating any cartridge in chamber, cylinder or attached magazine as loaded.
Some colleges (e.g. Univ. of Alabama) claim campus bans including parking lots and garages.

name: Alaska

permitless.notes: Anyone 21+ who can legally possess a firearm may carry concealed without a permit, but must immediately inform any officer on contact and let the officer secure the weapon. Under 21 concealed carry is a crime (limited defenses at home or while hunting/outdoors).

honors.notes: Statute treats any state's (or political subdivision's) concealed handgun permit holder as an Alaska permittee. Exception noted: Alaska has told Idaho it will only honor the Idaho Enhanced permit.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Alaska State Troopers (Department of Public Safety)
residentPermit.training: Handgun course required (AS 18.65.715); training valid 12 months
residentPermit.notes: Apply in person at a State Troopers office with an Alaska driver's license/ID, fingerprints and photo. $90 non-refundable fee. Decision within 30 days. Residency period: 90 days.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Alaska does not issue non-resident permits.

dutyToInform.notes: Anyone 21+ carrying a concealed deadly weapon must immediately inform a peace officer on contact and allow the officer to secure it (or secure it as directed) for the contact. Also applies when carrying in a vehicle.

vehicle.permitHolder: Same as without a permit: may carry a loaded handgun openly or concealed in the vehicle; must inform officers and follow securing instructions.
vehicle.noPermit: Anyone 21+ who can legally own a firearm may carry a loaded handgun openly or concealed in a vehicle. Must inform any officer on official contact; officer may take charge of it or direct you to secure it elsewhere in the vehicle.
vehicle.notes: State, cities and private parties may not ban possession in a vehicle or storage locked in a legally parked vehicle, except employers may bar it in secured restricted-access areas and posted lots within 300 ft. Minimum age to possess/transport unloaded and secured: 16.

magazineLimit.notes: Source found no higher-capacity magazine restrictions in Alaska law.

selfDefenseNotes: Text only lists justification statutes (AS 11.81.300-.450, incl. deadly force in self-defense and defense of premises) without describing castle doctrine or duty to retreat.

preemption.notes: Firearm and knife regulation reserved to the state; municipalities may not regulate possession, carry, transport, etc. unless a statute allows. Source notes municipal buildings may reportedly ban guns in posted 'prohibited areas'.

schools.notes: K-12 schools, grounds, parking lots and buses for school activities prohibited without permission of the school's chief administrator. Non-students 21+ may keep an unloaded firearm in the trunk or a closed container in a vehicle.

restAreas.notes: Text says carry is allowed in roadside rest areas.

stateParks.notes: Allowed in state parks, state/national forests and game management units. Parks on Army Corps of Engineers land are off-limits under federal law.

pollingPlaces.notes: The text does not address polling places.

airports.notes: Parking lot OK; terminal status unclear in the text (refers to admin rule 17 AAC 42.065).

bars.notes: Loaded firearm prohibited where liquor is sold for on-premises consumption. Defense if it is a concealed handgun in a designated restaurant and you do not drink.

churches.notes: The text does not address places of worship.

stateBuildings.notes: Prohibited in Alaska Court System courtrooms/offices and courthouses used only by courts and justice agencies. Source says municipal buildings may ban guns in posted 'prohibited areas' (statutory basis unclear).

prohibitedPlaces: K-12 schools, grounds, parking lots and school buses/activities (without administrator permission)
Places selling liquor for on-premises consumption (except restaurant without drinking)
Licensed child care facilities (other than private homes), incl. grounds and adjacent parking
Alaska Court System courtrooms and offices; courthouses used only by courts/justice agencies
State-funded domestic violence or sexual assault shelters
Another person's residence without an adult resident's express permission (concealed)
Assisted living homes for 6+ residents, child care centers, residential child care facilities, maternity homes
Army Corps of Engineers land (federal law)

noGunSigns.notes: Signs have no force of law except at places the law already makes off-limits. You must leave if asked, or face trespass charges.

openCarry.notes: Open carry legal without a permit. Source says the state minimum age is under 18, but federal law bars under-18 handgun possession. Off-limits places still apply.

notes: Duty to inform applies to everyone 21+ carrying concealed, with or without a permit.
Concealed carry under age 21 is a crime even though open carry is allowed.
Do not enter someone else's home carrying concealed without an adult resident's express permission.
Loaded = cartridge in chamber, magazine, clip or cylinder that is installed in or on the firearm.
During declared disasters, government may not ban, seize or restrict sale of firearms or ammunition.

name: Arizona

permitless.notes: Anyone 21+ who may legally possess a firearm may carry concealed without a permit, including in vehicles. Permitless carriers may NOT carry into any establishment serving alcohol for on-premises consumption.

honors.notes: Honors any state's permit valid in its issuing state if holder is legally present and not prohibited. Exception: only the Idaho Enhanced permit is honored, not the ID standard permit. Holder must be 21+ and not under felony indictment.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Arizona Department of Public Safety (Concealed Weapons Permit Unit)
residentPermit.training: Proof of firearms competence required (DPS/NRA course, hunter ed, military service, or another state's permit with training); no expiry on training
residentPermit.notes: Age 19 with current military service or honorable/general discharge. Apply online or by mail with 2 fingerprint cards; $60 fee. Allow 75 days. Permit term not stated in text.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Available by mail to US citizens from AZ DPS: request a packet, mail application, proof of firearms competence (e.g. DD-214 or another state's permit with training), 2 fingerprint cards and fee ($60). DPS prioritizes in-state residents.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to volunteer, but during a lawful stop/detention you must answer accurately if an officer asks whether you carry a concealed deadly weapon. Must show permit on request when carrying under a permit in a liquor establishment.

vehicle.permitHolder: May carry loaded, concealed or open, in a vehicle anywhere carry is legal.
vehicle.noPermit: Anyone 21+ who can legally own a handgun may carry it loaded and concealed in a vehicle without a permit. Those 18+ may possess/transport a handgun unloaded and secured. Text gives no glove box/console rule.
vehicle.notes: Property owners and employers generally may not ban firearms kept in your locked private vehicle and out of sight (exceptions: secured lots with storage, alternative parking, etc.). On K-12 grounds the gun must be unloaded and locked out of sight if you leave the vehicle.

magazineLimit.notes: The text mentions no magazine capacity limit.

selfDefenseNotes: Text lists justification statutes (ARS 13-401 to 13-421), incl. 13-418 defense of residential structure or occupied vehicle and 13-419 presumption, without describing them. Defensive display of a firearm (incl. verbal warning) is justified when force would be.

preemption.notes: Political subdivisions may not regulate possession, carry, transport, sale, storage, etc. of firearms or ammunition; violating ordinances are void, with civil penalties up to $50,000 and lawsuits allowed.

schools.notes: K-12 school grounds prohibited except the parking lot: firearm must be unloaded, and if you leave the vehicle it must be locked and out of sight. Universities (ASU/NAU/UA) bar weapons on campus except locked, hidden in private vehicles.

restAreas.notes: Text says carry is allowed in roadside rest areas (per AZ DPS).

stateParks.notes: Allowed in state parks, state/national forests and WMAs. Parks on Army Corps of Engineers land are off-limits under federal law.

pollingPlaces.notes: Prohibited at polling places on Election Day.

airports.notes: Text says parking lots and terminal OK (ARS 13-3119).

bars.notes: Permit holders (AZ or any state) may carry into places serving alcohol unless posted with the statutory 4-229 sign. Permitless carriers may not enter any such place armed, posted or not.

churches.notes: The text does not specifically address places of worship (general private-property sign rules apply).

stateBuildings.notes: Operators of public establishments/events may ask you to remove a weapon and must then provide secure on-site storage (not all comply). Correctional facilities incl. parking lots are off-limits.

prohibitedPlaces: K-12 school grounds (parking lot allowed only with unloaded firearm, locked out of sight if unattended)
Polling places on Election Day
Correctional facilities, including their parking lots
Commercial nuclear or hydroelectric generating stations
Any establishment or event whose operator reasonably requests removal (signs count)
Liquor-licensed on-sale premises posted with the 4-229 sign
Any on-premises alcohol establishment if carrying without a permit
Army Corps of Engineers land (federal law)

noGunSigns.notes: Any sign giving reasonable notice is enough; ignoring a sign or a verbal request can be criminal trespass. Liquor establishments must use the specific 4-229 sign (red-circle pictogram plus statutory wording).

openCarry.notes: Open carry legal without a permit at 18+. Open carriers without a permit cannot enter places serving alcohol. Same off-limits places apply.

notes: Concealed carry under 21 is a crime even with another state's permit; open carry allowed at 18.
Without a permit from AZ or another state, you cannot carry into restaurants/bars serving alcohol.
Idaho standard permits are not honored; only Idaho Enhanced.
Arizona does not define 'loaded'; source suggests no cartridge in chamber, cylinder or attached magazine.
Emergency powers cannot be used to add firearm or ammunition restrictions.

name: Arkansas

permitless.notes: Statute (2023) says no license is needed to carry concealed; carrying is only a crime with intent to use it unlawfully against a person. Text gives no specific permitless age; 18 is the stated minimum age to possess/transport a handgun.

honors.notes: Honors all other states' concealed handgun licenses, including non-resident ones. Out-of-state holders get the same privileges and restrictions as AR licensees. Campus carry needs an AR license with endorsement.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Arkansas State Police
residentPermit.training: Course from an ASP-registered instructor; apply within 6 months of training
residentPermit.notes: Age 18 for active duty, Guard/Reserve or honorably discharged veterans. 90-day residency (waived for active duty and spouses). Fee $88.25 (65+: $63.25). Enhanced endorsement needs extra training. Term not stated.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Only active duty military stationed in Arkansas (with a signed letter from the commanding officer) and their spouses may apply; contact the ASP Licensing Unit. Not available to other non-residents.

dutyToInform.notes: Licensees with a handgun must, when an officer asks for ID, show the license and photo ID and say they are licensed and armed. Must carry license whenever possessing a handgun. Text gives no duty for permitless carriers.

vehicle.permitHolder: May carry concealed in the vehicle, and may keep it in the vehicle or locked unattended vehicle in publicly owned parking lots (incl. K-12 and college lots, public buildings), except Correction lots.
vehicle.noPermit: Anyone who can legally possess a firearm may carry in a vehicle without a permit; carrying on a journey is presumed lawful. Text gives no glove box/trunk rules. Minimum age to possess/transport unloaded and secured: 18.
vehicle.notes: Law treats a vehicle as an extension of the home. Private employers must allow employees to keep lawful firearms out of sight in a locked private vehicle in the lot, with exceptions.

magazineLimit.notes: The text mentions no magazine capacity limit.

selfDefenseNotes: Text only lists justification statutes (5-2-601 to 5-2-621, incl. 5-2-620 force to defend persons and property within home) without describing them. Vehicle is defined as an extension of the home 'with any protections that conveys'.

preemption.notes: Cities/counties may not regulate ownership, transfer, transport, carry or possession of firearms, ammo, components or knives (except unsafe discharge), and may not adopt emergency gun ordinances.

schools.notes: No firearms on developed K-12 property, school buses or designated bus stops; licensees may keep a handgun in the vehicle in public parking lots. College campuses only with an AR license plus endorsement; dorm storage banned.

restAreas.notes: Former rest-area ban was repealed; text says carry is allowed.

stateParks.notes: Allowed, but posted park buildings (lodges, restaurants, visitor centers, offices, etc.) are off-limits. Parks on Army Corps land banned by federal law. City park carry for licensees except active sports fields, city buildings, leased event areas.

pollingPlaces.notes: The text does not address polling places.

airports.notes: Not inside the passenger terminal or sterile area; parking lot OK. Firearms encased for checking as baggage are allowed in the terminal.

bars.notes: Licensees may not carry into the portion of an establishment licensed for on-premises alcohol (or beer/light wine), except restaurants (as defined) unless posted.

churches.notes: Churches/places of worship are listed as off-limits, but each church may decide who may carry; churches can also post or give verbal notice.

stateBuildings.notes: Loaded firearms banned in publicly owned buildings and State Capitol grounds; any firearm banned in State Capitol and Justice Building. AR enhanced-endorsement holders may carry in many public buildings (not courtrooms, prisons, K-12).

prohibitedPlaces: Police, sheriff and State Police stations; Highway Police facilities
Detention facilities, prisons, jails and DYS residential treatment facilities incl. Correction parking lots
Courthouses and county buildings used for court or county offices; courtrooms
Meeting places of any government governing body; General Assembly meetings
State offices; publicly owned buildings (loaded firearms); State Capitol and Justice Building
Athletic events not related to firearms
Bar portions of alcohol-licensed establishments (except restaurants)
K-12 developed property, school buses and bus stops; school/college buildings and events (without endorsement)
Inside airport passenger terminals (except firearm encased for checking)
Churches/places of worship (unless the church allows)
Places prohibited by federal law
Permitted parades/demonstrations while participating
Places posted 'carrying a handgun is prohibited' or after verbal/written notice by a private owner
Posted firearm-sensitive areas at Arkansas State Hospital, UAMS and collegiate athletic events
Posted state park buildings and posted city/county parks; Army Corps of Engineers land

noGunSigns.notes: Posting each entrance with a notice readable from 10 ft that 'carrying a handgun is prohibited' bars licensees. Private owners may also give verbal/written notice; remaining or returning is a violation. Entering a private home requires telling the occupant you are armed.

openCarry.notes: Source says permitless concealed and open carry are legal for anyone who can legally possess a firearm (2018 appeals ruling on 5-73-120). Text gives no specific open-carry age.

notes: Licensees must carry their license whenever armed and disclose it when an officer asks for ID.
Campus carry at public colleges requires an Arkansas license with the enhanced endorsement; out-of-state permits do not qualify.
Licensees entering a private home must tell the occupant they are carrying.
Pepper spray allowed for self-defense up to 300 ml container.
Loaded = cartridge in a position to be fired by one manual operation of any mechanism.

name: California

permitless.notes: No permitless carry. A California-issued license is required to carry a loaded handgun, including in a vehicle.

honors.notes: California does not honor any other state's permit.

residentPermit.issuedBy: County Sheriff or city Chief of Police
residentPermit.training: Min. 16-hour course incl. live fire with each listed gun and written exam; 8 hours for renewal
residentPermit.notes: Source calls CA shall-issue only because 'justifiable need' was struck; many hurdles remain. Must be recorded owner of each listed gun. Psych exam possible. Decision within 120 days. Fees vary by county. Source's misc table says 18 but statute says 21.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Statute says a sheriff shall issue to non-residents 21+ with home-state license/ID who swear the county is their main CA destination, complete CA training and live fire for each listed gun. Source says a 2025 court ruling lets members of CRPA, GOA, GOC or SAF apply.

dutyToInform.notes: State law has no duty to inform on contact, but some issuing agencies add it as a license condition, which then must be obeyed. Licensees must carry the license and show it and the firearm to an officer on demand.

vehicle.permitHolder: Licensee may carry concealed per the license. At prohibited places (except nuclear sites and federal bans) may transport and store the gun in an approved locked lock box out of plain view, incl. in prohibited parking areas.
vehicle.noPermit: Handgun must be unloaded and in a locked container or the locked trunk; glove box and console do NOT count. Loaded carry in a vehicle requires a CA license. Rifles/shotguns must be unloaded; assault weapons need a locked container.
vehicle.notes: Minimum age to possess/transport unloaded and secured: 18. Police may inspect any firearm in a vehicle in public to check if loaded; refusing is probable cause for arrest. Loaded magazines in the same container have reportedly led to arrests.

magazineLimit.notes: Possessing, importing, buying or receiving magazines over 10 rounds is banned statewide (PC 32310). Text lists federal rulings (2019, 2020) holding the ban unconstitutional without giving its current status. SF, Sunnyvale and Oakland also ban them.

ammo: No ammo on K-12 school grounds unless locked in a vehicle container/trunk. At gun shows you may not hold a firearm and its ammo at the same time. San Francisco bans sale of Black Talon-type and LE-only ammunition. SF bans guns and ammo on county property.
selfDefenseNotes: Text only lists PC 195-199 (justifiable homicide), incl. 198.5 on force used within one's residence, without describing it. CA law lets people 18+ keep a loaded gun at home, temporary residence (e.g. hotel), campsite or business.

preemption.notes: State preempts only registration/licensing of commercially made firearms. Cities have their own bans (e.g. SF, Oakland, Sunnyvale magazine bans; SF county property ban), and local law can add off-limits places.

schools.notes: Gun-free school zones: K-12 grounds and within 1,000 ft. Licensees may carry within the 1,000 ft zone but not on school property, parking or adjacent sidewalks. Colleges/universities incl. parking are off-limits. Unlicensed: unloaded and locked in vehicle only.

restAreas.notes: Text says carry is allowed in roadside rest areas (per CHP).

stateParks.notes: Dept. of Parks and Recreation and Fish and Wildlife property off-limits except designated hunting areas. Game refuges off-limits. Public parks and athletic areas also banned. State/national forests: allowed.

pollingPlaces.notes: Polling places, vote centers and ballot counting/return sites plus adjacent streets/sidewalks. Open carry near election activity is presumed intimidation.

airports.notes: Buildings, property and parking areas controlled by an airport or passenger vessel terminal. Exceptions: gun in a locked lock box in a vehicle, or unloaded in a locked hard case for checking outside the sterile area.

bars.notes: Licensees may not carry anywhere liquor is sold for on-premises consumption (incl. parking), be in a place mainly serving alcohol, or drink at all while carrying. Source says no restaurant carry.

churches.notes: Places of worship and adjacent parking are off-limits unless the operator posts the DOJ-design sign (min 4x6 in) allowing licensees to carry.

stateBuildings.notes: State and local government buildings (incl. those with courtrooms), public meetings, State Capitol and grounds, legislative/constitutional offices and residences, and their parking areas.

prohibitedPlaces: K-12 schools and school zones (1,000 ft, except licensees outside school property)
Colleges and universities, incl. parking and common areas
Preschools and childcare facilities
State executive/legislative buildings and parking; State Capitol and grounds
Courthouses and court buildings incl. parking
Local government buildings and parking; public meetings
Jails, prisons, detention facilities incl. grounds and parking
Hospitals, mental health facilities, nursing homes, medical offices, urgent care
Public transit vehicles and transit facilities (unless unloaded in a lock box)
Places selling alcohol for on-premises consumption, incl. parking
Permitted public gatherings/special events and within 1,000 ft on adjacent streets
Playgrounds and youth centers and adjacent sidewalks
Public parks, athletic areas/facilities
State Parks and Fish and Wildlife land (except hunting areas); game refuges
Gambling venues: casinos, card clubs, bingo, horse racing facilities
Stadiums, arenas, collegiate/pro sporting and eSports events
Public libraries
Airports and passenger vessel terminals incl. parking
Amusement parks, zoos and museums
Nuclear facilities
Places of worship unless posted to allow licensees
Banks/financial institutions and their parking
Police, sheriff and CHP stations and parking
Polling places, vote centers and ballot counting sites
Picketing during labor disputes
Places banned by other state, federal or local law

noGunSigns.notes: General signs have no force of law except at statutory off-limits places; you must leave if asked. Note: the rule banning carry in private businesses unless posted as allowing it (26230(a)(26)) was struck down by the US Supreme Court.

openCarry.notes: Source says open carry is not legal in most instances. Sheriffs in counties under 200,000 people may issue a license to carry loaded and exposed in that county only. Openly carrying an unloaded handgun unlawfully is a nuisance.

notes: Licensees may carry only the guns listed on the license (max two at a time) and must be the recorded owner.
No drinking at all while carrying under a license; being under the influence is barred.
Magazines over 10 rounds banned (court challenges noted); registered assault weapons have strict transport rules.
Unlicensed travellers: handgun unloaded in a locked container (not the glove box or console).
Carrying a firearm while masked in public is a crime.

name: Colorado

permitless.notes: No permitless concealed carry, except anyone who may legally possess a handgun may carry it in a private vehicle for lawful use (not treated as concealed). Open carry without a permit is legal at 18+ with exceptions.

honors.notes: Honors only resident permits: holder must be 21+ and a resident of the issuing state, shown by that state's photo ID/driver's license carried with the permit. New CO residents may use a reciprocal home-state permit for up to 90 days. Only MN resident permit honored.

residentPermit.issuedBy: County Sheriff
residentPermit.training: In-person class, min. 8 hours incl. live fire and written exam (no online); valid 1 year; refresher class to renew
residentPermit.notes: Apply in person to sheriff of residence, secondary residence or business-property county. Fee: $52.50 state plus sheriff fee up to $100. Military stationed in CO and family count as residents. 90-day emergency permit possible at 18+.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Statute says only Colorado residents may apply; military on permanent duty orders in CO and their immediate family are treated as residents. Source notes some sheriff applications still reference non-residents.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to inform. Permittees must carry the permit and photo ID while carrying and produce both on an officer's demand. Officers may temporarily disarm a permittee during a lawful stop.

vehicle.permitHolder: May carry concealed in the vehicle. At school, college and certain government-building parking areas, the handgun may stay in the vehicle; if unattended, it must be stored per the vehicle storage law.
vehicle.noPermit: Anyone who may legally possess a handgun may carry it (loaded) in a private vehicle for lawful use incl. self-defense; it is not considered concealed. Outside the vehicle, open carry only. Rifles/shotguns: chamber must be unloaded.
vehicle.notes: Unattended: handgun in a locked hard-sided container out of view (locked glove box/console counts) in a locked vehicle. Locals cannot restrict carry in private vehicles while traveling. Gun reachable by a minor can be charged.

magazineLimit.notes: Selling, transferring or possessing magazines over 15 rounds (shotgun: over 28 in. tube or 8 shells detachable) is a misdemeanor unless owned continuously since July 1, 2013. Vail bans 21+ round magazines. Denver bans assault weapons.

selfDefenseNotes: Text lists 18-1-701 to 18-1-710, incl. 18-1-704.5 deadly force against an intruder, without describing them. It cites a 2020 CO Supreme Court case: improper to argue failure to retreat before using lethal force.

preemption.notes: Firearm regulation is a matter of state and local concern: local governments may pass stricter laws on sale, transfer and possession and may ban open or concealed carry in posted buildings/areas. Travel with a weapon in a private vehicle is preempted.

schools.notes: K-12, licensed child care centers, and public/private colleges, universities and seminaries prohibited. Permittees may keep a handgun in their vehicle on K-12 property and carry concealed in college/child care parking areas.

restAreas.notes: Text says carry is allowed in roadside rest areas.

stateParks.notes: Allowed in state parks, state/national forests and WMAs. Parks on Army Corps of Engineers land are off-limits under federal law. Cities may ban carry in posted parks.

pollingPlaces.notes: Open carry banned in polling locations and within 100 ft of drop boxes/polling buildings and central count facilities during voting. Permit does not authorize carry in violation of this law; quoted text only addresses open carry.

airports.notes: Denver International Airport: loaded firearms banned in the terminal and sterile/secured areas (city rule). Other airports not addressed.

bars.notes: Source says carry in restaurants serving alcohol is allowed (cites 18-12-106(1)(d)). Bars and drinking limits are not described in the text.

churches.notes: The text does not address places of worship.

stateBuildings.notes: Banned in General Assembly buildings, local government chambers/elected offices (unless locally allowed) and courthouses, incl. parking (permittees may carry concealed in parking). Also public buildings with security screening.

prohibitedPlaces: K-12 schools (permittee may keep handgun in vehicle)
Licensed child care centers
Public and private colleges, universities and seminaries (parking allowed for permittees)
General Assembly buildings, chambers, hearing rooms and member offices, incl. parking
Local government chambers, meetings and elected officials' offices (unless locally allowed)
Courthouses and buildings used for court proceedings
Public buildings with permanent security screening and weapon check
Polling locations, within 100 ft of drop boxes and central count facilities (open carry)
Denver International Airport terminal and sterile areas
Posted local-government buildings, parks or areas banned by ordinance
Places prohibited by federal law; Army Corps of Engineers land
Public transportation facilities (open carry / loaded without permit)

noGunSigns.notes: Source says 'YES/NO': local-government signs posted under an ordinance have force of law. Private signs have no force of law except at statutory off-limits places, but you must leave if asked or face trespass.

openCarry.notes: Legal without a permit at 18+, with exceptions: banned in Denver, on public transit, and in posted local-government buildings/areas. Banned at polling places and near drop boxes.

notes: Only RESIDENT permits of listed states are honored; non-resident permits (e.g. Utah or Florida non-resident) are not valid.
Magazines over 15 rounds are banned unless owned since July 2013.
Unattended vehicle: handgun must be in a locked hard-sided container out of sight in a locked vehicle.
Cities (e.g. Denver, Boulder) have their own bans: Denver bans open carry and assault weapons; Boulder bans possession under 21.
Firearm and ammo within reach of anyone under 18 (e.g. in a console) has led to charges.

name: Connecticut

permitless.notes: No permitless carry. A Connecticut permit is required to carry a handgun, including loaded in a vehicle. Minimum age to possess/transport a handgun is 21.

honors.notes: Connecticut does not honor any other state's permit.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Local police chief/first selectman (temporary permit), then State Police (DESPP) state permit
residentPermit.training: Approved course at least NRA Basic Pistol level, incl. CT law on storage, use and carry; taken within 2 years of applying
residentPermit.notes: Statute says 'may issue' on suitability, but source says CT works like shall-issue. Local decision within 8 weeks. Source lists $70 temporary permit; statute says $140 for the state permit plus FBI fee; renewal $70.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Apply by mail to CT State Police Special Licensing and Firearms Unit (email SLFU.OOS@ct.gov for a packet with unique service code). About $145 plus fingerprints. NRA course plus CT law sign-off; home-state issuer must certify good standing.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to inform. Must carry the permit while carrying and show it when an officer with reasonable suspicion of a crime who has observed the handgun asks.

vehicle.permitHolder: May carry the handgun loaded in the vehicle under the permit. If the vehicle is unattended (no one 21+ nearby), handgun must be in the trunk, a locked safe or a locked glove box.
vehicle.noPermit: A permit is required to carry a loaded handgun in any vehicle. Travellers passing through under federal law: unloaded, with gun and ammo not accessible from the passenger area; if no trunk, in a locked container other than the glove box or console.
vehicle.notes: SUV/hatchback/wagon cargo areas do not count as a trunk. Rifles/shotguns may not be loaded (barrel, chamber or magazine) in a vehicle. Unattended storage violation is a class A misdemeanor.

magazineLimit.notes: Buying, importing or possessing magazines over 10 rounds is banned unless declared/registered. Declared ones may be carried under a permit only inside a pre-4/5/2013 handgun, extending under 1 in. below the grip, with max 10 rounds.

ammo: Text mentions a state ammunition certificate (29-38n) without details. Firearms must be stored locked or kept on/near the person (29-37i). Source notes many restrictions on firearms and magazines that may be brought into CT.
selfDefenseNotes: Text only lists justification statutes (53a-16 to 53a-23) and an AG opinion titled 'Castle Doctrine' without describing them. Discharging a firearm in lawful self-defense is not unlawful discharge.

preemption.notes: No preemption law. Towns may restrict concealed carry, e.g. Woodbridge bans firearms on all town property and New London bans them at demonstrations/special events. Many towns ban guns in parks, not always posted.

schools.notes: Felony to possess a firearm on public or private K-12 school property or at school-sponsored activities when not 'licensed or privileged' to do so (text does not clarify whether a carry permit qualifies).

restAreas.notes: Text says carry is allowed in roadside rest areas (per CT State Police).

stateParks.notes: Carrying firearms in state parks and forests is banned except as authorized by DEEP (e.g. some hunting). State preserves and WMAs also off-limits; Bluff Point Coastal Reserve banned. National forests listed as NO.

pollingPlaces.notes: The text does not address polling places.

airports.notes: Source says 'No laws found' on airport carry.

bars.notes: Source says carry in restaurants serving alcohol is allowed; bars are not separately addressed in the text.

churches.notes: The text does not address places of worship (private owners may prohibit carry).

stateBuildings.notes: Banned in General Assembly buildings/offices and hearing locations and in courthouses (Judicial Branch). An executive order bars state employees, contractors and vendors from bringing firearms to state worksites.

notes: No reciprocity: you need a CT permit (non-residents can apply by mail) to carry at all.

name: Delaware

permitless.notes: Concealed carry without a license is a felony. Open carry without a permit is legal (see openCarry).

honors.notes: Idaho: Enhanced permit only. North Dakota: Class 1 only. South Dakota: Enhanced only. Non-resident permits from honored states are honored. AG publishes list each Jan 15.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Superior Court (apply via county Prothonotary; AG reviews)
residentPermit.training: Approved gun course after approval, completed/enrolled within 90 days; training valid 5 years
residentPermit.notes: Residents only. Applicant names are published in a newspaper. AG may interview. License covers other deadly weapons too. Term not stated in text.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Only a limited temporary license at AG discretion for a short-term employment-related need; expires in 30 days, not renewable, max 3 issued. No general non-resident permit.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to inform. Law doesn't expressly require carrying the permit, but an instructor reports the AG says you must have it on you.

vehicle.permitHolder: Permit holders (and holders of honored permits) may carry concealed in a vehicle.
vehicle.noPermit: Firearm must be clearly visible, e.g. on the seat or dash. Under the seat, glove box or console counts as concealed (felony).
vehicle.notes: Loaded firearms banned in vehicles for purposes of taking wildlife (hunting). Minimum age to possess/transport a handgun without a permit is 21 (HB 451).

magazineLimit.notes: Magazines over 17 rounds banned. Exemption covers holders of DE Superior Court-issued permits; text says it likely does not cover non-residents carrying on honored permits.

selfDefenseNotes: Text only lists justification statute titles (11 Del. C. 461-475, incl. §469 person unlawfully in dwelling and §475 immunity) without content.

preemption.notes: State preempts county/municipal firearm laws, but municipal ordinances before 7/4/1985 are grandfathered. Counties/cities may ban guns in police stations and their buildings, but concealed-permit holders are exempt.

schools.notes: K-12 school property and school vehicles. Permit holders exempt only if firearm stays in a vehicle; locked container/rack in a vehicle also exempt. Weapons banned on school buses.

restAreas.notes: Text says carry allowed at road-side rest areas.

stateParks.notes: Carry allowed outside designated areas (offices, visitor centers, pools, etc.). Only DE resident permit holders may carry in designated areas. Same for state forests. Not on Army COE-owned park land.

pollingPlaces.notes: Banned at polling places on Election Day (incl. early voting), from 2 hours before polls open to 2 hours after close. Parking areas excluded.

airports.notes: Text says no laws found.

bars.notes: Text says carry allowed in restaurants that serve alcohol; nothing specific on bars.

stateBuildings.notes: Courthouses, police stations, prisons and detention facilities prohibited. County/municipal buildings may be posted, but concealed permit holders are exempt.

name: District of Columbia

permitless.notes: No permitless carry. Loaded carry (including in a vehicle) requires a DC-issued license; all firearms must be registered in DC.

honors.notes: DC does not honor any other state's permit/license.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Metropolitan Police Department (Chief / Firearms Registration Section)
residentPermit.training: Firearms training course by a Chief-certified instructor; training valid 2 years; may be preapproved if training completed within 45 days
residentPermit.notes: Must register the pistol to be carried in DC. Fee $75. MPD says processing is 4-5 days once training and documents are in hand. License term not stated in text.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Non-residents apply to the MPD Firearms Registration Section, must meet all resident eligibility rules and register any firearm to be carried in DC. Out-of-state training may count, but a DC-certified trainer must certify training in DC firearms and self-defense law. Fee $75.

dutyToInform.notes: On an investigative stop, licensee (and any licensee with them) must disclose the pistol, present license and registration certificate, identify its location and comply with orders including pat-down.

vehicle.permitHolder: Licensee may carry concealed on their person in a vehicle; pistol must be entirely hidden from public view. When approaching a prohibited place, secure it unloaded and inaccessible per transport law.
vehicle.noPermit: Firearm must be unloaded and neither firearm nor ammo accessible from the passenger compartment (trunk). If no separate compartment, use a locked container other than glove box or console.
vehicle.notes: Federal safe passage (926A) covers only passing through; stopping other than for gas/emergency puts you under DC law. Loose ammo components (empty cases, primers, bullets) count as ammunition.

magazineLimit.notes: Possession of magazines holding more than 10 rounds is banned (except attached .22 rimfire tubular magazines).

ammo: Only registered firearm owners (and certain others) may possess ammunition in DC; empty cases, primers, bullets and powder count as ammo. Licensees may not carry restricted pistol bullets.
selfDefenseNotes: Text lists no DC deadly force statutes ('No laws found'); refers only to MPD self-defense instructions for trainers.

preemption.notes: No preemption law; DC is a single jurisdiction so district law (plus federal rules) applies throughout.

schools.notes: Buildings, grounds and adjacent parking of childcare, preschools, K-12 schools and colleges/universities. Exception: driving in to drop off/pick up a child if pistol is secured in vehicle before leaving it.

restAreas.notes: Text marks road-side rest areas as '?'.

stateParks.notes: Text marks parks/forests as '?'. National Mall/Tidal Basin memorials and federal areas are prohibited.

pollingPlaces.notes: Prohibited at a polling place while voting is occurring.

airports.notes: No airports in DC; Reagan and Dulles are in Virginia (see VA rules).

bars.notes: Prohibited where alcohol is served for on-premises consumption, but restaurants with C/R or D/R (and certain other) licenses are exempt. No drinking or impairment while carrying.

churches.notes: Presumed prohibited unless posted allowing carry or owner personally permits it in advance.

stateBuildings.notes: Buildings or offices occupied by the DC government or its agencies.

notes: Every carried firearm must be registered in DC; carry both license and registration certificate.

name: Florida

permitless.notes: Anyone who meets license eligibility criteria may carry concealed without a license. Age lowered from 21 to 18 by 2026 court ruling. Must carry valid ID and show it to police on demand ($25 fine).

honors.notes: Honors all states' resident permits; no non-resident permits. Holder must be a U.S. resident with permit in immediate possession. New FL residents' permits valid 90 days.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Florida Dept. of Agriculture and Consumer Services, Division of Licensing
residentPermit.training: Certificate of firearms competency incl. live fire; military ID accepted; no expiry on training
residentPermit.notes: Apply online, in person at regional offices or approved tax collectors, or by mail. Must live in the U.S. License covers handgun, electric weapon, tear gas gun, knife or billie.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Same process as residents (online or mail to FDACS). Non-residents must submit paper fingerprint cards taken by a law enforcement agency; any notary may sign. Must live in the U.S.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to inform. Permitless carriers must carry valid ID and display it on an officer's demand.

vehicle.permitHolder: Licensed or permitless-eligible persons may carry concealed on their person in a vehicle.
vehicle.noPermit: Persons 18+ in lawful possession may keep a handgun securely encased (glove box locked or not, snapped holster, gun case, closed box) or not readily accessible, but not on their person. Long guns may be anywhere for lawful use.
vehicle.notes: Employers/businesses cannot ban firearms locked in private vehicles in their parking lots (exceptions: schools, prisons, nuclear and defense sites, etc.).

selfDefenseNotes: Text lists Chapter 776 section titles only (e.g. 776.013 home protection with presumption of fear; 776.032 immunity) without their content.

schools.notes: K-12, career centers, colleges (public or private), school buses, bus stops and school events. Firearm may stay in a vehicle per 790.25(4), but districts may waive this for student parking.

stateParks.notes: Also state forests and WMAs. Savannas State Reserve bans all firearms; Army COE-owned parks off limits.

airports.notes: Not inside passenger terminal or sterile area, except a firearm encased for checking as baggage.

bars.notes: Prohibited in the portion of an alcohol-licensed establishment primarily devoted to serving alcohol; restaurant dining areas allowed.

churches.notes: License holders may carry on religious property, even shared with a school, unless the institution forbids it.

stateBuildings.notes: Prohibited in police/sheriff/highway patrol stations, courthouses, courtrooms, legislative meetings and local/school board meetings.

name: Georgia

permitless.notes: Any 'lawful weapons carrier' (eligible for a GA license, incl. non-residents but for residency) may carry open or concealed. Age 18-20 allowed with proof of basic training and active duty or honorable discharge.

honors.notes: Honors all states' permits incl. non-resident permits; must follow GA law. One quoted version of 16-11-126(d) limits this to states that honor GA licenses - text is inconsistent.

residentPermit.issuedBy: County Probate Court (county of residence)
residentPermit.notes: Age 18-20 if completed basic training and active military or honorably discharged. Online application in many counties but must sign in person. Fees vary by county (e.g. $73.25-$80). Covers other weapons too.

nonResidentPermit.notes: No non-resident license. Military personnel stationed in Georgia may apply at the Probate Court of the county where stationed. Non-residents can carry permitless if otherwise eligible.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to inform. Police may not detain someone solely to check whether they are licensed or a lawful weapons carrier. Carrying ID (and military ID if 18-20) recommended.

vehicle.permitHolder: Lawful weapons carriers (licensed or eligible) may carry/transport a handgun or long gun in any private passenger vehicle, open or concealed.
vehicle.noPermit: No license needed for eligible persons to carry open or concealed in a vehicle, but per Hubbard v. State only in your own vehicle or with permission of the person controlling it. Anyone not prohibited may carry a long gun.
vehicle.notes: Firearm in a vehicle (under control, locked compartment/container/rack) is OK in parking facilities of government buildings, courthouses, jails and places of worship. Employers can't search locked private vehicles in their lots (with exceptions).

selfDefenseNotes: Text lists justification statute titles only (16-3-20 to 16-3-28, incl. 16-3-24 'Property, Duty to Retreat' and 16-3-24.2 immunity; 51-11-9 civil immunity for defense of habitation) without content.

preemption.notes: Counties, cities and state agencies may not regulate possession, carry, transport, licensing or registration of firearms; locals may limit discharge.

schools.notes: K-12 school safety zones, functions and school buses prohibited (OK in vehicle when picking up/dropping off a student or parked). Public colleges allowed except athletic venues, student housing, childcare, dual-enrollment classes, faculty/disciplinary offices.

stateParks.notes: All parks, historic sites, recreation areas incl. their buildings, forests and WMAs. Not where federal law prohibits (e.g. Army COE land, developed TVA areas).

pollingPlaces.notes: Within 150 feet of a polling place while elections are being conducted.

airports.notes: Allowed in parking and terminal areas outside screening; prohibited at or beyond the security checkpoint (license holder who leaves immediately when notified is not guilty).

bars.notes: Text says carry allowed in restaurants serving alcohol; nothing specific on bars.

churches.notes: Prohibited unless the place of worship's governing body permits lawful weapons carriers. Violation by a lawful carrier: no arrest, fine up to $100.

stateBuildings.notes: Allowed in government buildings open to the public without security screening; prohibited where entry is screened by security incl. a POST-certified officer. Courthouses and jails/prisons prohibited.

notes: A lawful weapons carrier who notifies security on arrival at an off-limits location and follows their directions is exempt.

name: Hawaii

permitless.notes: No permitless carry. Carrying a loaded firearm on a public highway or in a vehicle without a HI license is a class B felony.

honors.notes: Hawaii does not honor any other state's permits/licenses.

residentPermit.issuedBy: County Chief of Police
residentPermit.training: In-person course with live fire by a chief-certified instructor; training valid 4 years
residentPermit.notes: Apply in person; must be registered owner of the firearm(s) to be licensed. Fee $150 ($50 renewal), waivable for hardship. Valid statewide; concealed or unconcealed licenses exist. Covers firearms only.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Text conflicts: page says non-resident availability is UNKNOWN and law never states residency, yet quoted HRS 134-9(a)(5) requires the applicant be a resident of the State.

dutyToInform.notes: Anyone carrying who is stopped (incl. as driver or passenger) must immediately disclose the firearm, and on request show its location, the license and proof of registration.

vehicle.permitHolder: Licensee may carry the licensed pistol/revolver in a vehicle. A firearm left unattended in a vehicle must be locked in a safe/secure container out of sight; a locked trunk or glove box alone is not enough.
vehicle.noPermit: No loaded firearm in a vehicle or on a public highway without a HI license (class B felony; vehicle may be forfeited). Text doesn't detail unloaded transport rules.
vehicle.notes: All firearms brought into Hawaii must be registered and inspected by county police within 5 days of arrival. Minimum age to possess/transport a handgun is 21.

magazineLimit.notes: Detachable pistol magazines over 10 rounds banned (unless permanently modified to 10). Court challenges noted but ban still in effect per text.

selfDefenseNotes: Text lists only justification statute titles (HRS 703-300 to 703-310). Licensees have absolute liability for injury/damage from an unjustified discharge.

restAreas.notes: Allowed at road-side rest areas, but not in buildings.

churches.notes: State law silent; Hawaii County ordinance bans carry in churches unless the administrator permits.

stateBuildings.notes: Any state/county building or office and adjacent grounds/parking (court order limits parking ban to lots shared with non-government entities).

name: Idaho

permitless.notes: Permitless concealed carry only for U.S. citizens or current U.S. military members, 18+, not disqualified. Others may carry concealed without a license only outside city limits, at home/business or on permitted property.

honors.notes: Honors all other states' resident and non-resident permits; permit must be in your physical possession.

residentPermit.issuedBy: County Sheriff
residentPermit.training: Proof of familiarity: hunter ed, NRA or similar course, military service, etc. Enhanced: 8-hour in-person course with 98 live rounds within the prior 12 months
residentPermit.notes: Fee $20 ($15 renewal) plus fingerprint/material costs (~$64 total). Standard and Enhanced licenses. Provisional license for ages 18-20 expires at 21. Issued within 90 days. Covers other weapons.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Apply to a county sheriff (some won't issue to non-residents); application in person or by mail, ~90 days, pick up in person. Enhanced license requires a current permit from your home state.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to inform. Visitors carrying on another state's permit must have it in physical possession.

vehicle.permitHolder: Permit holders may carry concealed in a vehicle.
vehicle.noPermit: Eligible U.S. citizens/military 18+ may carry concealed in a vehicle. Others: weapon in plain view, or concealed in vehicle (one quoted version says only if unloaded), or unloaded and cased.
vehicle.notes: Text quotes two versions of 18-3302(4)(c): 'any deadly weapon concealed in a motor vehicle' vs 'a firearm that is not loaded and is concealed in a motor vehicle'. Employers may post parking lots.

name: Illinois

permitless.notes: No permitless carry. An Illinois concealed carry license is required to carry; open carry is not legal.

honors.notes: Illinois honors no other state's permit. Limited exception: a non-resident eligible to carry at home (with a home-state permit if that state issues one) may keep a concealed handgun in their vehicle if it stays in the vehicle.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Illinois State Police
residentPermit.training: 16 hours from an ISP-approved instructor (up to 8 hours of approved prior training may count)
residentPermit.notes: Valid FOID card required (the CCL also serves as the FOID). Apply online or by phone. Fee $150. ISP has 90 days to decide (+30 days if no fingerprints submitted).

nonResidentPermit.notes: Only residents of AR, ID, MS, NV, TX and VA may apply, and they must hold their home-state license. 16 hours ISP-approved training, notarized affidavit, $300 fee. Apply online to ISP (phone may also work).

dutyToInform.notes: During an investigative/traffic stop, licensees and non-residents carrying in a vehicle must disclose the firearm and show the license if the officer asks, say where the gun is, and let the officer secure it.

vehicle.permitHolder: Licensees may carry a loaded concealed handgun on or about their person in the vehicle. Non-residents eligible at home may carry a concealed handgun in the vehicle only if it stays in the vehicle.
vehicle.noPermit: Unloaded and enclosed in a case (residents need a FOID), broken down, or not immediately accessible. Text advises travellers without a home-state permit to carry it unloaded and cased in the trunk or SUV rear.
vehicle.notes: In prohibited-site parking lots, a licensee may keep the gun in the vehicle or store it cased in a locked vehicle or locked container out of view. Leaving the car with it is allowed only to put it in the trunk. Exception: nuclear sites.

name: Nevada

permitless.notes: The text does not describe permitless concealed carry. Open carry is legal without a permit at 18+.

honors.notes: Only ID enhanced, MS enhanced, ND Class 1 and SD enhanced permits. Michigan was dropped 10/24/2025. Out-of-state permits stop being valid if the holder moves to NV and lacks a NV permit after 60 days.

residentPermit.issuedBy: County Sheriff (Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Dept in Clark County)
residentPermit.training: Sheriff-approved firearm safety course, or one from law enforcement, a college or a national instructor-certifying organization; must cover handguns and NV law
residentPermit.notes: Age 18-20 allowed for active military or honorably discharged veterans. LVMPD is about $100 initial and $65 renewal. One permit covers all handguns the holder owns. Fingerprints and photo required.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Apply in person at any NV county sheriff, same process as residents. Training must take place in Nevada (some counties require it in that county). About $97 initial, $62 renewal; valid 5 years.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to inform. Permittees must carry the permit and ID while carrying concealed and show both if a peace officer asks ($25 civil penalty).

vehicle.permitHolder: May carry concealed under the permit. Source cites no vehicle-specific restrictions on handguns.
vehicle.noPermit: A handgun on the person must be clearly visible. A handgun under or on the seat or in the glove box is not 'on the person' and is allowed.
vehicle.notes: Loaded rifles or shotguns (round chambered) are illegal in a vehicle on or along a public way. Minimum age to possess and transport a handgun is 18.

magazineLimit.notes: Text mentions no magazine capacity restriction.

selfDefenseNotes: Statute list includes NRS 200.120 'Justifiable homicide; no duty to retreat under certain circumstances' and 200.130 (reasonable fear required; rebuttable presumption in some cases). Details not given.

preemption.notes: The Legislature reserves all firearm regulation. Counties, cities and towns may only regulate unsafe discharge; conflicting ordinances are void and those harmed can sue for damages.

schools.notes: Banned on property of public/private schools, child care facilities and the Nevada System of Higher Education, and in their vehicles, unless written permission is obtained.

restAreas.notes: Roadside rest areas: YES.

stateParks.notes: State parks, state/national forests and WMAs: YES. Parks on Army Corps of Engineers lake land fall under the federal ban.

pollingPlaces.notes: Not addressed in the text.

airports.notes: Parking lot OK. No concealed carry in public buildings on airport property (terminal). Source notes it is told open carry may be legal in public areas outside security.

bars.notes: Bars are not addressed. Restaurant carry: YES (no law prohibits it).

churches.notes: Not addressed in the text.

stateBuildings.notes: Permittees may carry in public buildings, except ones with metal detectors or no-firearms signs at every public entrance (unless written permission), and buildings on airport, school or child-care property.

name: New Hampshire

permitless.notes: Anyone not prohibited from possessing a firearm (resident, non-resident or alien) may carry openly or concealed, loaded or unloaded, without a license. No permitless age is stated; open carry minimum is 18.

honors.notes: Only honors permits issued by the holder's home state. Permitless carry makes reciprocity largely moot for people eligible to possess.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Local police chief or sheriff
residentPermit.notes: $10. Bring a state photo driver's license or ID. Source says the law lists no minimum age. Submit renewals within 30 days of expiration; no renewal notice is sent.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Issued by the NH State Police Permits and Licensing Unit, 33 Hazen Dr, Concord NH 03305. Apply by mail. $100, valid 5 years. A home-state permit is not required.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to inform. The source recommends carrying a state-issued ID.

vehicle.permitHolder: May carry in a vehicle, loaded or unloaded, openly or concealed.
vehicle.noPermit: Anyone not prohibited may carry or transport a firearm in a vehicle without a license, loaded or unloaded, openly or concealed.
vehicle.notes: On an OHRV or its trailer, firearms must be unloaded, except handguns carried by non-prohibited people. Employers receiving public funds can't ban employees' guns locked out of sight in their vehicles.

magazineLimit.notes: No magazine capacity restrictions found.

selfDefenseNotes: Source cites a NH Supreme Court case (1/2024) holding there is no duty to retreat in a lethal-force attack. Lists RSA 627 justification statutes, including defense of premises and civil immunity.

preemption.notes: The state has sole authority over firearms, ammunition and knives; municipal ordinances are void. Localities keep only normal zoning of firearm businesses.

schools.notes: School carry is not addressed in the text.

restAreas.notes: Roadside rest areas: YES.

stateParks.notes: State parks, state/national forests and fish and game refuges: YES. Parks on Army Corps of Engineers lake land fall under the federal ban.

pollingPlaces.notes: Not addressed in the text.

airports.notes: Source found no state law barring carry in airport parking lots or terminals. Secure/sterile areas are not addressed.

bars.notes: Bars are not addressed. Restaurant carry: YES.

churches.notes: Not addressed in the text.

stateBuildings.notes: Courtrooms and court-used areas are banned (class B felony); whole court-only buildings past security. Corrections property is off-limits. No other state building limits are stated.

prohibitedPlaces: Courtrooms and areas used by a court (entire building if court-only, beyond the entrance/security area)
Department of Corrections property

noGunSigns.notes: Signs have no legal force unless the place is listed as off-limits by law. You must leave if asked; refusing is trespass.

openCarry.notes: Legal without a license for anyone who can legally possess; minimum age 18. Preemption bars local bans.

notes: Carrying a gun into a courtroom or court-used area is a class B felony, whether licensed or not.
NH does not honor non-resident permits from other states, but permitless carry applies to non-residents.
The permit covers firearms only, not other weapons.
Concealed defensive carry while hunting is allowed except during muzzleloader season and while shining.
'Loaded' (fish and game law) means a round in the chamber. A NH Supreme Court case says ammo must be in the firearm, not just near it.

name: New Jersey

permitless.notes: No permitless carry. Carrying a concealed handgun in public without a NJ permit and proof of liability insurance is a 4th-degree crime.

honors.notes: New Jersey does not honor any other state's permit.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Municipal chief of police (NJ State Police Superintendent if no local chief)
residentPermit.training: Required: online course, in-person classroom and range qualification with a certified instructor, including deadly-force law
residentPermit.notes: $200 fee. Four unrelated reputable references who have known you 3+ years; fingerprints. Admin code still lists 'justifiable need', but the source says the Supreme Court struck that down.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Non-residents apply to the NJ State Police Superintendent (online through the NJSP portal). $200 fee; fingerprints, training and references required as for residents.

dutyToInform.notes: Permit holders stopped or detained must at once tell the officer about a handgun on them or in the vehicle, and show the permit. FOPA travellers passing through need not notify.

vehicle.permitHolder: May carry concealed in a holster on the person. A handgun left in a parked car must be unloaded in a closed, fastened case or gunbox out of sight, or locked unloaded in the trunk.
vehicle.noPermit: No loaded handgun in a vehicle without a NJ permit. Others must keep it unloaded in a closed, fastened case or gunbox, or locked in the trunk. A NJ permit or FPIC is generally needed even to transport.
vehicle.notes: Passing through is OK under federal 18 USC 926A: unloaded, with gun and ammo out of reach (locked container if no trunk; not the glove box or console), and legal at origin and destination.

magazineLimit.notes: Ban still in effect while a court stay stands. The quoted statute (2C:39-1y, 2025) bans over 10 rounds; source narrative still says over 15. Tube magazines holding only .22 rimfire are exempt.

ammo: Hollow points are banned for carry. They may be bought and kept at home or on your land, at a range, or while travelling between those places. Armor-piercing ammo is banned except for licensed C&R collectors.
selfDefenseNotes: Text lists the NJ justification statutes (2C:3-1 to 2C:3-11) without summarizing them.

residentPermit.notes: Age 21, or no minimum for honorably discharged veterans. Requires good moral character, in-person interview, 4 character references, household info, and 3 years of social media accounts. Decision due within 6 months.

selfDefenseNotes: Text only lists the Penal Law Article 35 justification statutes (35.00-35.30); it does not describe castle doctrine or duty to retreat.

preemption.notes: New York has no state preemption law for firearms, ammunition or accessories.

vehicle.noPermit: A loaded firearm may be carried without a permit if it is in plain view. It is illegal to have a weapon both concealed and readily accessible (under the seat, in a bag, etc.); this includes long guns.
vehicle.notes: NC law does not specifically address vehicle transport; guidance is from the NC Sheriffs' Association. Local governments cannot bar storing a firearm in a vehicle on their grounds.

magazineLimit.notes: Text lists no magazine capacity restriction.

selfDefenseNotes: Text lists 14-51.2 (home, workplace and motor vehicle protection; presumption of fear of death or serious harm), 14-51.3 (defense of person) and 14-51.4, without detailing duty to retreat.

pollingPlaces.notes: Text does not address polling places.

churches.notes: Not generally addressed. Where a church shares property with a school (not a college), permittees may carry outside school hours or while attending worship, unless posted.

name: North Dakota

permitless.notes: Since 8/1/2023 anyone 18+ who may legally possess a firearm can carry concealed without a license, residents and non-residents alike. Must carry a valid driver's license or state ID. Permitless carry must be concealed.

honors.notes: Honors only permits issued by the holder's home state (by driver's license) from the listed states (HB 1293, 2021). A permit ND issues or honors is required to open carry.

dutyToInform.notes: Permit holders: no duty, but show license on request. Permitless carriers must disclose the firearm. Statute says 'if the officer inquires'; AG and Handgunlaw.us say on any in-person contact.

vehicle.noPermit: Anyone 18+ not barred from a Class 2 license and carrying a valid driver's license/ID may keep a loaded handgun, or loaded rifle/shotgun when not hunting, in a vehicle. Otherwise loaded firearms in vehicles are an infraction.
vehicle.notes: A gun under the seat or in the glove box counts as concealed. Employers can't bar lawful firearms locked in private vehicles in parking lots (exceptions: K-12 schools, prisons, etc.).

magazineLimit.notes: Text lists no magazine capacity restriction.

selfDefenseNotes: Text only lists Chapter 12.1-05, including 12.1-05-07.1 (presumption of fear of death or serious injury for deadly force) and 12.1-05-07.2 (civil immunity), without detail.

restAreas.notes: Carry allowed at publicly owned rest areas, including buildings and restrooms.
