pollingPlaces.notes: Not specifically addressed; polling places in publicly owned buildings would fall under the public building ban.

airports.notes: Publicly owned terminals are off-limits as public buildings; parking lots OK. Handgunlaw.us advises not carrying in any terminal.

bars.notes: Barred in the part of an establishment set aside for buying and drinking alcohol, and at bingo sites. Restaurant areas open to under-21s are OK.

churches.notes: Prohibited unless you are a licensed/reciprocity concealed carrier approved by the church's religious leader or governing body.

stateBuildings.notes: Publicly owned or operated buildings; Capitol grounds and buildings without written Highway Patrol approval.

prohibitedPlaces: Schools and school-sponsored events on school property
Churches/places of worship (unless approved by church leadership for licensees)
Publicly owned or operated buildings
State Capitol grounds and buildings
Bar/liquor-sale areas of establishments and bingo gaming sites
State wildlife refuges
Publicly owned airport terminals
Correctional facilities (parking-lot law exception)

noGunSigns.notes: Signs have no force of law except on places already off-limits by statute, but you must leave if asked or face trespass charges.

openCarry.notes: Residents and non-residents need a permit ND issues or honors to open carry; permitless carry must be concealed.

notes: Permitless carriers must have a driver's license or state ID (or a digital image) and show it on request; violation is a $20 noncriminal offense.
Honored out-of-state permits must be from the holder's state of residence.
A ND license also covers dangerous weapons, not just firearms.
Pepper spray and single-shot stun guns/Tasers need no license; multi-shot projectile Tasers do.
During emergencies, officials may not restrict lawful firearm possession or carry, or suspend carry permits.

name: Ohio

permitless.notes: A 'qualifying adult' (21+, not prohibited, meets most license criteria) may carry a concealed handgun without a license wherever licensees can, under the same rules. Active-duty military with qualifying training: 18.

honors.notes: Non-residents temporarily in Ohio may carry on any state's license. An Ohio resident's out-of-state license is honored only from reciprocity/comparable states, otherwise for 6 months after moving in.

residentPermit.issuedBy: County Sheriff
residentPermit.training: 8 hours, including at least 2 hours in-person range/live-fire (rest may be online)
residentPermit.notes: Apply at sheriff with application, training certificate, photo, fingerprints; fee about $67 (varies by county), renewal about $50. Fees waived for military/veterans. Training valid 3 years.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Only for non-residents employed in Ohio, who apply like residents with proof of employment. Sheriffs may issue an emergency license to someone with justifiable need present in Ohio. Licenses of people who move away can't be renewed.

dutyToInform.notes: When stopped, must disclose a concealed or loaded handgun before or when the officer asks. Keep hands in sight, stay in the vehicle, don't touch the gun, and obey orders. Applies to permitless carriers too.

vehicle.permitHolder: Licensees may have a loaded handgun in a vehicle. On a stop: disclose when asked, stay in the vehicle, keep hands visible, don't touch the gun. Keep it inaccessible to children or prohibited persons (e.g., on your person).
vehicle.noPermit: Qualifying adults (21+) without a license are treated the same as licensees. Text does not detail rules for others beyond the definition of 'unloaded' (loaded magazines kept in a separate closed enclosure or inaccessible compartment).
vehicle.notes: Businesses and employers can't bar licensees from keeping firearms/ammo locked in their private vehicle. Firearms may be left in a locked vehicle in the State Capitol and Riffe Center garages.

magazineLimit.notes: No magazine limits in Ohio; the old 31+ round machine-gun definition was removed.

selfDefenseNotes: Statutes 2901.09 and 2307.601 provide no duty to retreat in your residence or anywhere you have a lawful right to be. Property owners have self-defense immunity under 2305.40.

preemption.notes: State law (9.68) preempts local firearm, ammunition and knife regulation, with civil damages and fees against cities that violate it.

schools.notes: School safety zones are off-limits, unless a licensee leaves the handgun in a vehicle and locks it when exiting. Colleges also off-limits, except a locked vehicle or institution-authorized carry.

restAreas.notes: Carry allowed at roadside rest areas; buildings used as rest facilities/restrooms are OK.

stateParks.notes: Allowed in state parks, forests and WMAs; park buildings are off-limits except restrooms, shelters and comfort stations. Army Corps of Engineers park land is off-limits.

pollingPlaces.notes: Text does not address polling places.

airports.notes: Terminal and parking lot OK; prohibited past security or in other access-restricted areas.

bars.notes: May carry in Class D liquor premises if not drinking or under the influence and not posted. No consuming alcohol while carrying.

churches.notes: Prohibited unless the place of worship posts or otherwise permits carry.

stateBuildings.notes: Government facilities off-limits unless used primarily as a shelter, restroom, parking or rest facility; courthouses/courtrooms also off-limits.

prohibitedPlaces: Police stations, sheriffs' offices, Highway Patrol posts, BCI premises
Prisons, jails and detention facilities
Airport areas past security or with restricted access
State mental health / developmental disability institutions and facilities for mentally ill persons
School safety zones (except handgun left in locked vehicle)
Courthouses and buildings with courtrooms
College/university premises (except locked vehicle or authorized)
Places of worship unless they permit carry
Child day-care centers (if posted)
Government facilities (other than shelters, restrooms, parking, rest facilities)
Class D liquor premises if drinking or under the influence
State park and forest buildings (except comfort facilities)
Places where federal law bans handguns
Private property posted against firearms

noGunSigns.notes: Violating a posted sign is criminal trespass (4th-degree misdemeanor); posted parking lots only carry civil trespass liability. Posted child-care homes/centers: aggravated trespass.

openCarry.notes: Open carry is legal without a license at 21+ (18 for trained active-duty military).

notes: Duties on stops (disclose when asked, hands visible, don't touch gun) apply to licensees and permitless carriers.
Concealing a deadly weapon other than a handgun is illegal.
Some Ohio cities regulate stun devices.
Landlords can't bar licensed tenants from keeping handguns at their residence.
During declared emergencies the state may not restrict lawful firearms; expiring licenses are extended.

name: Oklahoma

permitless.notes: Anyone 21+ not barred from firearms may carry concealed or open without a license. Ages 18-20 qualify if military members/veterans or honorably discharged. Must have a license, military ID, driver's license or state ID while carrying.

honors.notes: Recognizes any valid concealed or unconcealed carry permit/license from another state. Visitors from permitless states are covered under their home state's law.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation (OSBI), application processed through county sheriff
residentPermit.training: Firearms safety and training course with qualification on the type of pistol carried (certificate valid 3 years)
residentPermit.notes: Age 18 for military members/veterans. Fees: $100 (5 yr) / $200 (10 yr) new; $85 / $170 renewal. Apply online or at sheriff, who takes fingerprints. Residency = OK driver's license/ID.

nonResidentPermit.notes: No non-resident licenses. Military members and spouses on permanent orders in Oklahoma may apply like residents.

dutyToInform.notes: Handgunlaw.us says no duty, but statutes require disclosing a firearm during any arrest, detainment or traffic stop, and on officer demand in a vehicle. Out-of-state licensees must disclose on contact with any peace officer.

vehicle.permitHolder: May carry a loaded handgun concealed or openly in a vehicle. Must disclose the firearm on an arrest, detainment or traffic stop.
vehicle.noPermit: Anyone 21+ not prohibited from firearms may transport a loaded or unloaded firearm in a vehicle at any time, open or concealed. Ages 18-20 may transport only unloaded firearms (open or concealed).
vehicle.notes: Failing to identify a firearm when an officer demands during a stop: citation up to $100. Businesses and employers can't bar firearms locked in vehicles in parking lots (except for felons).

magazineLimit.notes: Handgunlaw.us found no high-capacity magazine restrictions in Oklahoma law.

ammo: Under the Self-Defense Act, a carried handgun loaded with restricted bullets or ammo larger than .45 caliber is a prohibited weapon (criminal penalty plus $500 fine).
selfDefenseNotes: Deadly force is presumed reasonable against unlawful forcible entry into a dwelling, occupied vehicle, business or place of worship (1289.25). Defensive display of a firearm is justified when force is reasonably necessary.

preemption.notes: State preempts the entire field of firearms, knives, ammo and air guns; cities may only regulate discharge and issue certain citations. Lawful carry can't be charged as disorderly conduct.

schools.notes: K-12 schools, school buses, colleges, universities and technology centers. Licensees may keep a handgun hidden in a locked vehicle in school parking. Private schools may allow licensees by policy.

restAreas.notes: Carry allowed at roadside rest areas.

stateParks.notes: Allowed in parks, forests, wildlife refuges, WMAs and fairgrounds, but not in government buildings there. Army Corps of Engineers parks are off-limits. Municipal zoos/parks run by trusts or nonprofits: concealed only.

pollingPlaces.notes: Text does not address polling places specifically; government buildings open to the public are off-limits.

airports.notes: Terminals owned by a government entity are off-limits; parking lots OK. Handgunlaw.us advises not carrying in any terminal.

bars.notes: Prohibited where alcohol sales are the primary purpose of the business. Allowed in restaurants where alcohol is not the main business. No drinking while carrying.

churches.notes: Not listed as off-limits, but a place of worship may ban firearms and must post signs if open to the public.

stateBuildings.notes: City, county or state buildings/offices used to do business with the public, plus courthouses, jails and detention facilities. Adjacent grounds and parking are OK; cities may allow concealed carry in their buildings.

prohibitedPlaces: City, town, county and state government buildings/offices open to the public (cities may allow)
Courthouses, courtrooms, prisons, jails and detention facilities
Public and private K-12 schools and school buses (limited exceptions)
College, university and technology center property (except parking/authorized)
Public sports arenas during professional events (unless event holder allows)
Gambling venues (unless owner allows)
Government-secured events with fencing, officers and metal detectors
Establishments whose primary business is selling alcohol
Government-owned airport terminals
Oklahoma State Fair and Tulsa State Fair grounds during the fairs (may be prohibited)
Public sports fields/seating during school, college, pro or Olympic events (may be prohibited)
Any other place prohibited by law

noGunSigns.notes: Signs only let the owner deny entry or remove you; refusing to leave once police are called is a misdemeanor, fine up to $250.

openCarry.notes: Legal without a license at 21+ (18+ for military members/veterans). Handgun must be in a holster, or long gun in a sling/scabbard/case.

notes: Carry a handgun license, military ID, driver's license or state ID at all times while carrying, and show it on demand.
Carrying ammo larger than .45 caliber or restricted bullets in a Self-Defense Act handgun is prohibited.
Pointing a firearm at someone is a felony unless in self-defense, defense of property or lawful defensive display.
Cherokee Nation ordinance restricts carrying weapons; Handgunlaw.us reads it as allowing lawful carry.
During declared emergencies, officials can't suspend lawful sale, possession or carry of firearms and ammo.

name: Oregon

permitless.notes: Oregon is not listed among permitless-carry states; concealed carry requires an Oregon Concealed Handgun License. Open carry without a license is legal at 18+ subject to local loaded-firearm ordinances.

honors.notes: Oregon does not honor any other state's permit/license.

residentPermit.issuedBy: County Sheriff
residentPermit.training: Handgun safety course (police/NRA-certified instructors, security, military, competition) or ODFW hunter education course; online course certificate from Oregon State Sheriffs Association accepted
residentPermit.notes: Must be US citizen (or legal resident noncitizen with 6 months county residency and declared intent to naturalize). Fees: $100 initial + $15 fingerprint check to State Police; $75 renewal. Fingerprints required.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Only for residents of contiguous states (WA, CA, ID, NV) with a compelling business interest or other demonstrated need; may-issue at sheriff's discretion, some sheriffs won't issue. Apply to any Oregon sheriff; reportedly two references required.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to inform, but the license must be carried whenever carrying a concealed handgun.

vehicle.permitHolder: License holders may carry a concealed, loaded handgun in a vehicle.
vehicle.noPermit: A handgun may be carried openly/visible, or if concealed it must not be readily accessible (outside the passenger compartment; if no such storage exists, in a closed locked glove box/console/container with key removed). Motorcycles/ATVs: locked container or trigger lock.
vehicle.notes: Cities/counties may regulate loaded firearms in public places (including vehicles) for those without a license; e.g. Portland bars loaded guns and even loaded magazines in the car.

magazineLimit.notes: Text does not state a statewide magazine capacity limit.

selfDefenseNotes: Text only lists the deadly force statutes (ORS 161.190-161.270) without summarizing castle doctrine or duty to retreat.

preemption.notes: State preempts firearm regulation, but cities/counties may regulate discharge and possession of loaded firearms in public places by people without a license; some pre-1995 county discharge ordinances survive.

schools.notes: Schools/colleges are public buildings; licensees have an affirmative defense unless the school board adopts a policy (posted at entries and online) removing it.

restAreas.notes: Carry allowed in roadside rest areas.

stateParks.notes: Allowed in state parks, state/national forests and WMAs; not on Army Corps of Engineers-owned park land.

airports.notes: Parking lots OK; passenger terminals of airports with over 1 million boardings/year (e.g. Portland) are off limits even to licensees.

bars.notes: Restaurants serving alcohol: carry allowed (no law against it). Text does not address bars specifically.

stateBuildings.notes: Licensees are exempt from the public-building ban, except the Capitol buildings and local government meeting buildings that adopt a posted policy; court facilities are prohibited.

prohibitedPlaces: Court facilities (and local courts by judge's order)
State Capitol buildings
Passenger terminals of airports with over 1 million boardings/year
School grounds whose board adopts a no-carry policy
City/county/district official-meeting buildings with an adopted, posted policy
Department of Corrections facility grounds
Racecourses
Commission for the Blind property
Tribal property without tribal court license
Public buildings (for those without a license)

noGunSigns.notes: Signs have no force of law except on places named in statute; you must leave if asked or face trespass.

openCarry.notes: Legal at 18+ without a license, but cities/counties may ban loaded carry in public places by non-licensees; all public buildings are off limits to unlicensed open carriers.

notes: Oregon honors no other state's permit; non-residents can only get a license if from a bordering state and the sheriff agrees.
Local ordinances (e.g. Portland) may ban loaded firearms in public, including in vehicles, for people without an Oregon license.
Oregon licenses are not honored on property of the nine federally recognized tribes, including casinos.
Portland bans tear gas weapons and stun guns except small OC/tear-gas aerosols (4 oz or less) and stun guns for self-defense by non-felons 18+.
Permit covers firearms only; concealed carry for defense while hunting is allowed with a license.

name: Pennsylvania

permitless.notes: Concealed carry and carry in any vehicle require a license. Open carry on foot without a license is legal at 18+.

honors.notes: Only resident permits honored. Idaho: Enhanced permit only. North Dakota: Class 1 only. Utah and West Virginia: regular permits only. PA residents must hold a PA license to carry in PA.

residentPermit.issuedBy: County Sheriff
residentPermit.notes: No training required. Bring PA DL/ID and two references; $20 fee; sheriff has 45 days. Some sheriffs add residency periods (up to 90 days) or other requirements. 45-day temporary emergency license available for imminent danger.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Apply in person at a county sheriff that issues to non-residents (some won't). Must hold your home-state permit if your state issues them (Vermont excepted). Bring copy of home permit, DL, two references; $20 for 5 years.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to inform, but licensees must produce the license on lawful demand of an officer when carrying concealed or in a vehicle.

vehicle.permitHolder: Holders of a PA license or an honored license may carry a loaded firearm in a vehicle, openly or concealed.
vehicle.noPermit: Carrying a firearm in any vehicle without a license is a crime (felony or first-degree misdemeanor) unless an exception in 18 §6106 applies; text points to federal 926A transport (unloaded, not accessible from passenger compartment). Possession/transport of unloaded, secured handgun allowed at 18+.
vehicle.notes: Per 18 §6106(b)(11), a person with a valid license from any other state may carry in a vehicle. Debate exists about unloading before taking a gun into a motel or friend's home overnight.

magazineLimit.notes: No state limit stated; a court ruled Pittsburgh's magazine ban violates state preemption.

selfDefenseNotes: Text only lists justification statutes (18 §501-510) without summarizing castle doctrine or duty to retreat.

preemption.notes: Strong state preemption upheld by PA Supreme Court (11/2024), but cities of the first class (Philadelphia) have exemptions to some parts.

schools.notes: Weapons banned in buildings, grounds and transport of K-12 public, private and parochial schools; courts allow an 'other lawful purpose' defense.

stateParks.notes: Allowed in state parks (concealed only), forests and WMAs for license holders; Philadelphia executive order bans guns at city rec centers, fields, playgrounds and pools.

airports.notes: Parking lot and non-sterile terminal areas OK.

bars.notes: Restaurants serving alcohol: carry allowed (no law against it). Bars not specifically addressed.

stateBuildings.notes: Court facilities prohibited (must be posted; free lockers provided). Department of State leased premises at One Penn Center, Harrisburg prohibited.

prohibitedPlaces: Court facilities (posted; lockers available)
K-12 schools, school grounds and school transport
Detention facilities, correctional institutions and mental hospitals
Department of State leased premises (One Penn Center, Harrisburg)
Philadelphia rec centers, athletic courts, fields, playgrounds and pools (executive order; likely preempted)
Public streets/property during a declared emergency (unless licensed)

noGunSigns.notes: No force of law except where state law names the place; must leave if asked or face trespass.

openCarry.notes: Legal at 18+ without a license on foot; license needed to carry in a vehicle. Philadelphia's license requirement for open carry was ruled unconstitutional 6/25/2025.

notes: Any firearm carried in a vehicle (loaded) requires a license; open carry without a license does not extend to vehicles.
Only RESIDENT permits of honored states are accepted; carrier must be 21+.
During a declared emergency, only licensees (or exempt persons) may carry on public streets or property.
Stun guns may be carried for self-defense if labeled with/accompanied by written instructions.
Permit covers firearms only; concealed carry for defense while hunting is allowed.

name: Rhode Island

permitless.notes: A license is required to carry a pistol or revolver on the person (visible or concealed) or in a vehicle, except at home, place of business or own land.

honors.notes: No other state's permit is honored for carry. Exception: holders of any state's valid permit may carry in a vehicle while merely transporting through RI with no intent to stay.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Local city/town police (concealed only); Attorney General (concealed or open, may-issue on showing of need)
residentPermit.training: Qualify with a certified instructor: 195/300 with 30 rounds slow fire at 25 yards, same or larger caliber than carried; valid 1 year
residentPermit.notes: Local permit requires 'good reason to fear injury or other proper reason' and suitability; RI Supreme Court says locals must issue or deny. Typical: $40 fee, notarized app, 3 notarized reference letters, letter of reasons, fingerprints.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Non-residents 21+ with a carry permit from another state may apply to a city/town (e.g. Foster PD issues to holders of any state's permit). $40; must pass the proof-of-ability shooting qualification; pick up in person.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to inform, but carrying a firearm is treated as evidence of unlawful carry unless you show a valid permit, so carry it on you.

vehicle.permitHolder: RI permit holders may carry a pistol/revolver in a vehicle. Holders of any other state's permit may carry loaded only while passing through without intent to stay.
vehicle.noPermit: Carrying a pistol or revolver in a vehicle without a license is prohibited (1-10 years). Possession/transport of an unloaded, secured handgun at 18+ is referenced.
vehicle.notes: Loaded rifles or shotguns (including loaded magazines) are unlawful on public highways, roads and trails.

magazineLimit.notes: Manufacture, sale, purchase or possession of feeding devices holding more than 10 rounds is banned (except .22 rimfire tubular magazines); up to 5 years prison.

selfDefenseNotes: Text only lists deadly force statutes (§11-8-8, §12-17-17 to 19) without summarizing them.

preemption.notes: Control of firearms and ammunition rests solely with the state, except as provided in the firearms chapter.

schools.notes: Banned on K-12 public/private school grounds, school-event areas and school transport. Colleges not covered. Exception: unloaded firearm in locked container/rack in a vehicle.

stateParks.notes: Prohibited in state parks, conservation management areas, state/national forests and WMAs.

airports.notes: Text says no airport laws found.

bars.notes: Restaurants serving alcohol: allowed. Carrying while intoxicated or under the influence of alcohol/narcotics is illegal.

prohibitedPlaces: K-12 school grounds, school-sponsored event areas and school transportation
State parks and conservation management areas
State/national forests
Wildlife management areas
Anywhere while intoxicated or under the influence

noGunSigns.notes: No force of law except where state law names the place; must leave if asked or face trespass.

openCarry.notes: Only Attorney General-issued permits allow open carry; locally issued permits are concealed-only. Open carry is rare.

notes: Rhode Island honors no out-of-state permits except for passing through in a vehicle without stopping to stay.
Magazines over 10 rounds are banned to possess.
Statute bans stun guns but a federal court struck that part down (3/15/2022); pepper spray OK at 18+.
Loaded long guns (or with loaded magazines) are illegal on public roads and trails.
Issuance type: header says shall-issue, but local permits require a stated proper reason and AG permits are may-issue on showing of need.

name: South Carolina

permitless.notes: Anyone 18+ who may legally possess a handgun may carry openly or concealed, loaded or unloaded, on the person or in a vehicle without a permit (2024 Act 111).

honors.notes: Statute honors permits of residents of reciprocal states that require a background check and training (SLED list), and automatically honors GA and NC; SC no longer publishes a list. Honored permits cover handguns only. Permitless carry at 18 makes this mostly moot.

residentPermit.issuedBy: SLED (State Law Enforcement Division)
residentPermit.training: Handgun course within 3 years incl. SC law, safety, storage, holster use, retention, de-escalation and 25 live rounds; free SLED course offered in every county
residentPermit.notes: No SLED fee; fingerprints max $5. Apply online with IdentoGo fingerprinting or by mail; processing up to 90 days.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Only for non-residents who own real property in SC (assessor-signed form SLED R-168) or military stationed in SC; same application, training and SLED process as residents; no fee.

dutyToInform.notes: The former must-inform requirement was repealed by H.3594 (2024).

vehicle.permitHolder: May carry loaded, openly or concealed, anywhere in the vehicle.
vehicle.noPermit: Same as permit holders: anyone not prohibited may carry or store a firearm loaded or unloaded anywhere in a vehicle, occupied or not.
vehicle.notes: On school/college property the firearm must stay in an attended or locked vehicle in a closed glove box, console, trunk or closed container. Capitol grounds parking: locked in vehicle, not readily accessible.

selfDefenseNotes: Protection of Persons and Property Act presumes reasonable fear when using deadly force against someone unlawfully entering a residence, occupied vehicle or business, with immunity provisions. Case-law self-defense elements include being without fault and having no other probable means of avoiding danger.

preemption.notes: Localities may not regulate transfer, ownership, possession, carrying or transport of firearms/ammo, but may temporarily restrict open carry at permitted public events (rallies, fairs, parades) with posted signs.

schools.notes: Prohibited on K-12, college and university property without express permission, except locked/attended vehicle storage in a closed compartment or container.

restAreas.notes: Interstate highway rest areas exempted from the public-building ban.

stateParks.notes: Allowed in state parks, state/national forests and WMAs.

pollingPlaces.notes: Prohibited at polling places on election days.

airports.notes: Publicly owned airports: not in the terminal (publicly owned building); parking lot OK.

bars.notes: May carry into businesses serving alcohol for on-premises consumption only if not drinking and not posted; leave if asked. Violation can revoke permit 5 years.

churches.notes: Prohibited in churches/religious sanctuaries unless express permission is given by church officials.

stateBuildings.notes: Prohibited in any publicly owned building without permission of authorities; surrounding public parking lots/garages are OK per AG opinion.

prohibitedPlaces: Law enforcement, correctional and detention facilities
Courthouses/courtrooms while court is in session
Polling places on election days
Offices/meetings of county, school district, municipal or special district governing bodies
School or college athletic events not related to firearms
Daycare and preschool facilities
Places where federal law prohibits carry
Churches without express permission
Hospitals, clinics, doctors' offices and medical facilities unless authorized
Another person's residence without permission
Premises posted with compliant 'NO CONCEALABLE WEAPONS ALLOWED' signs
K-12, college and university property (except secured in vehicle)
Publicly owned buildings without permission
Public transportation buses
Bars/restaurants if consuming alcohol

noGunSigns.notes: Signs must meet exact specs (8x12 in, 'NO CONCEALABLE WEAPONS ALLOWED', handgun silhouette, at each entrance 40-60 in high). Violation chargeable as trespass; second offense revokes permit 1 year.

openCarry.notes: Legal for anyone who can legally possess a firearm (18+); open carry alone is not reasonable suspicion. Localities may temporarily restrict it at permitted events.

notes: Permitless carry at 18 for anyone legally able to possess a handgun.
Do not drink while carrying in a place serving alcohol; posted restaurants are off limits.
Properly sized signs have force of law; a generic sign does not meet the statute.
Out-of-state permits are honored for handguns only, not other weapons.
Weapons are prohibited on public transit buses and charter buses.

name: South Dakota

permitless.notes: Since 7/1/2019 anyone 18+ who can legally possess a firearm may carry openly or concealed without a permit. Carrying state ID is recommended.

honors.notes: SD repealed its reciprocity statute; no permit is needed, so the source says it technically honors all permits though the law doesn't say so. Campus-carry law refers to 'reciprocal permits' without listing them.

residentPermit.issuedBy: County Sheriff (official permit issued by Secretary of State)
residentPermit.training: Regular/Gold: none. Enhanced: qualifying handgun course within 12 months, fingerprints; renewal needs live fire plus use-of-force and law-change instruction
residentPermit.notes: Three types: regular, gold card, enhanced (21+; 'restricted enhanced' for 18-20). 30 days county residency. Fees eliminated by SB 212 (2022), though text also cites a $50 enhanced renewal fee. Temporary permit within 5 days.

nonResidentPermit.notes: No non-resident permits, except active-duty military and spouses with a South Dakota home of record.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to inform; never lie to an officer.

vehicle.permitHolder: May carry loaded, openly or concealed, in a vehicle.
vehicle.noPermit: Anyone 18+ who can legally possess a firearm may carry a handgun in a vehicle, loaded, openly or concealed, without a permit.
vehicle.notes: Permit holders may keep a pistol in their vehicle on K-12 school premises and secure/retrieve it there.

magazineLimit.notes: No magazine capacity restrictions found.

selfDefenseNotes: 2021 law (HB1212) provides no duty to retreat for force/deadly force in defense of person, dwelling and property, a presumption of reasonable fear against unlawful entry, and immunity.

preemption.notes: Counties, townships and municipalities may not regulate firearms/ammo; violating ordinances are void and AG must act. State agencies may not restrict carry by rule.

schools.notes: Prohibited on public K-12 premises, vehicles and buildings, except enhanced permit holders 21+ with principal's written permission and any permit holder inside a vehicle. Public colleges must allow enhanced/reciprocal permit holders.

stateParks.notes: Allowed in state parks, forests and WMAs; not on Army Corps of Engineers-owned land.

airports.notes: Text says no law found.

bars.notes: Restaurants serving alcohol: allowed (no law against it). Bars not specifically addressed.

churches.notes: Text only notes the school-weapons law does not apply to churches or their nonpublic schools.

stateBuildings.notes: County courthouses prohibited. State Capitol prohibited except enhanced permit holders who notify the Highway Patrol 24 hours ahead (not Supreme Court chamber or secured offices).

prohibitedPlaces: Public K-12 school premises, buildings and vehicles (limited exceptions)
County courthouses
State Capitol (unless enhanced permit and 24-hour notice to Highway Patrol)
Designated hazardous/secure areas or special events with metal detectors on public college campuses

noGunSigns.notes: No force of law; must leave if asked or face trespass.

openCarry.notes: Legal for anyone 18+ who can legally possess a firearm.

notes: Permitless carry at 18; permits still issued for reciprocity in other states.
Enhanced permit is only valid when carried with government photo ID.
Enhanced permit not renewed within 30 days after expiration is invalid and must be reapplied for.
During declared emergencies, government may not restrict or seize firearms.
No chemical spray, stun gun or magazine restrictions found.

name: Tennessee

permitless.notes: Anyone 18+ who lawfully possesses a handgun may carry openly or concealed where lawfully present. Permitless carriers are barred from some places permit holders may go (parks, campgrounds, greenways, trails, 'permit only' posted buildings).

honors.notes: Any facially valid out-of-state handgun/firearm/weapons permit is honored as a TN permit, for handguns only; permit must be in possession while carrying. New TN residents must get a TN permit within 6 months.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Tennessee Department of Safety (Driver Services Centers)
residentPermit.training: Enhanced: Tennessee handgun safety course (certified school) unless exempt; Concealed: lesser training. Training valid 12 months
residentPermit.notes: Two tiers: Enhanced ($100; $65 military/honorable veteran) and Concealed Handgun Carry Permit ($65, concealed only, not valid at any school/university). Lifetime enhanced available. 30-day residency; fingerprints; up to 90 days.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Only for permit holders from non-reciprocal states employed in TN 30+ hrs/week for 6 consecutive months; must obtain TN enhanced permit within the following 6 months. Issued by Department of Safety.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to inform. When carrying where/how a permit is required, the permit must be on you and displayed on an officer's demand.

vehicle.permitHolder: May carry loaded in a motor vehicle or boat; may store in parking areas if kept from view (locked in trunk, glove box or interior when away from vehicle).
vehicle.noPermit: Anyone not prohibited from possessing firearms who lawfully possesses the vehicle or motorized boat may carry a loaded firearm in it. Permitless carriers (18+) may also use the parking-lot storage law.
vehicle.notes: Does not apply to employer-owned vehicles with a written no-firearms policy. Nonstudent adults may keep a firearm in their vehicle on school property if not handled.

magazineLimit.notes: No magazine capacity restrictions found.

selfDefenseNotes: Text only lists justification statutes (39-11-601 to 622, incl. self-defense and deadly force by private citizens) without summarizing castle doctrine or duty to retreat.

preemption.notes: State preempts the whole field of firearm, ammunition and knife regulation; locals may only regulate their own employees' carry, discharge (as authorized) and range locations. Adversely affected persons may sue.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Texas Department of Public Safety
residentPermit.training: 4-6 hours classroom (may be online), written exam and shooting proficiency, taught in Texas by a DPS-certified instructor
residentPermit.notes: 18 for military members/veterans; page says 18-20 now eligible after an unappealed court ruling. Online application, IdentoGo fingerprints. Fee $40 (discounts exist). Training certificate valid 2 years.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Apply online or by mail to Texas DPS. Needs a handgun proficiency certificate from a Texas course taught inside Texas, color copy of home-state ID, and IdentoGo fingerprints.

dutyToInform.notes: License holders carrying must show their handgun license along with ID when an officer asks for ID. Text says there is no penalty for not informing. No stated duty for permitless carriers.

vehicle.notes: Minimum age to possess/transport a handgun in a vehicle without a license is 18. Licensed holders and lawful possessors may keep guns locked in their private vehicles in employer parking lots, with exceptions.

selfDefenseNotes: Text only lists the Penal Code Chapter 9 justification sections (9.31 self-defense, 9.32 deadly force, 9.41-9.42 property) without summarizing them.

restAreas.notes: Roadside rest area carry allowed.

stateParks.notes: Allowed in state parks, state/national forests and WMAs. Parks on Army Corps of Engineers land are off limits under federal law.

pollingPlaces.notes: Prohibited on polling place premises on election day or during early voting.

bars.notes: Prohibited where 51%+ of income is on-premises alcohol sales (red 51% sign). Restaurants serving alcohol allowed unless posted.

churches.notes: Per an AG opinion listed, churches must be posted to be off limits.

stateBuildings.notes: Courts/court offices and open meetings of governmental bodies are prohibited. Government entities may not post other property against license holders unless state law bans carry there.

name: Utah

permitless.notes: 21+ who may lawfully possess firearms may open or concealed carry loaded without a permit. 18-20 without a permit may only carry openly in limited ways (loaded handgun in a vehicle; unloaded firearm on a public street).

honors.notes: Utah honors a concealed carry permit issued by any other state or county, including non-resident permits.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Utah Bureau of Criminal Identification (BCI), Dept. of Public Safety
residentPermit.training: BCI-certified firearms familiarity course, completed before applying
residentPermit.notes: Provisional permit available for ages 18-20. Requires fingerprint card, photo, background check. Online renewal available. Training valid 1 year.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Apply the same way as residents to BCI, with a course from a Utah-certified instructor (offered nationwide). If your home state honors Utah's permit, you must hold its permit first. Provisional (18-20) available.

dutyToInform.notes: No legal duty to inform; Utah DPS recommends telling the officer immediately. Law does not require carrying the permit while carrying.

vehicle.notes: Lawfully present = you possess the vehicle or have the possessor's consent. Employers/owners generally cannot ban locked, hidden guns in parked vehicles (exceptions: schools, government, religious orgs).

selfDefenseNotes: Text only lists deadly force statutes (76-2-401 to 76-2-407, incl. defense of habitation and persons on real property) without summarizing them.

restAreas.notes: Allowed per Utah Highway Patrol.

stateParks.notes: Allowed in state parks, state/national forests and WMAs. Army Corps of Engineers land is off limits under federal law.

airports.notes: Terminal and parking lots OK; secure area prohibited.

bars.notes: No statute bars permit holders from bars, but it is illegal to possess a firearm while intoxicated (same standard as DUI).

churches.notes: Allowed unless the house of worship gives notice (signs, personal notice, announcement or publication); violating notice is an infraction.

stateBuildings.notes: Prohibited in posted secure areas, and courthouses/courtrooms, mental health or correctional facilities that ban firearms by rule with notice at entrances.

name: Vermont

nonResidentPermit.notes: Vermont does not issue permits.

restAreas.notes: Roadside rest area carry allowed.

stateParks.notes: Allowed in state parks, forests and WMAs (park rules govern discharge, not carry). Army Corps of Engineers land off limits under federal law.

pollingPlaces.notes: Prohibited at polling places and walks leading to them on election day, and town clerk's office during approved early voting; firearm stored in a vehicle is exempt.

prisons, jails, houses of correction, secure correctional facilities
secure mental health facilities (incl. Mendota maximum security, Wisconsin Resource Center)
county, state and federal courthouses; municipal courtrooms in session
beyond airport security checkpoints
K-12 school grounds
posted government buildings, college buildings, private property and special events
Army Corps of Engineers property

noGunSigns.notes: Signs at least 5x7 inches posted at entrances make carrying a trespass. Parking areas are exempt if the gun stays in the vehicle.

openCarry.notes: Open carry legal at 18+ without a license; localities cannot ban it. Off-limits places still apply.

notes: No general non-resident license; visitors need a permit Wisconsin honors to carry concealed, including in a vehicle.
Florida and Virginia resident permits are not honored; only their non-resident permits are.
Licensees may not carry on K-12 school grounds.
Stun guns/electric weapons require a carry license (felony otherwise outside home/business).
Only OC or CS gel pepper spray is legal; no tear gas or mace.

name: Wyoming

permitless.notes: US residents (any state) who meet permit eligibility rules and may lawfully possess may carry concealed without a permit. HB 96 (7/1/2026) lowered the age to 18; older notes on the page still say 21.

honors.notes: Honors valid statewide permits from states that recognize Wyoming permits. Out-of-state permits do not unlock K-12 or college carry, which is limited to Wyoming-issued permits.

residentPermit.issuedBy: Wyoming Division of Criminal Investigation (Attorney General), applied for through the county sheriff
residentPermit.training: Proof of firearm familiarity: NRA or WY LE academy course, LE/security course, competition or military experience, or state/NRA-certified instructor course
residentPermit.notes: 6 months' WY residency required unless you hold an honored permit. Fees DCI $64 + sheriff $15 new; renewal DCI $45 + $5. Training valid 6 months. Out-of-state military can apply without appearing.

nonResidentPermit.notes: Wyoming does not issue non-resident permits.

dutyToInform.notes: No duty to inform, but permit holders must carry permit and ID while carrying concealed and show both when an officer requests.

vehicle.permitHolder: Permit holders may carry concealed in a vehicle.
vehicle.noPermit: Anyone 18+ who may lawfully possess may carry a handgun, loaded or unloaded, concealed or open, in a vehicle without a permit.
vehicle.notes: Wyoming law does not define 'loaded'.

magazineLimit.notes: Text found no magazine capacity restrictions.

selfDefenseNotes: Text lists W.S. 6-2-602 'Use of force in self defense; no duty to retreat' and 6-1-204 civil immunity for justified force, without details.

preemption.notes: State preempts all regulation of firearms, accessories and ammo; no state agency or local government may regulate carry or possession except as the chapter allows.

schools.notes: Only holders of a Wyoming-issued permit may carry concealed in public K-12 and college facilities and alcohol-free school athletic events. Permitless and out-of-state permit carriers may not. Students barred.

restAreas.notes: Allowed per Wyoming Highway Patrol.

stateParks.notes: Allowed in state parks, forests and WMAs. Army Corps of Engineers land off limits under federal law.

airports.notes: Concealed carry allowed in public airport areas not restricted by federal law; sterile areas prohibited.

bars.notes: Concealed carry prohibited in the portion of a licensed establishment primarily devoted to serving alcohol. Restaurants that serve alcohol allowed.

stateBuildings.notes: Concealed carry allowed in public buildings, government and legislative meetings (permitless included). Courtrooms, law enforcement facilities and jails excluded. Entities may ban open carry.

prohibitedPlaces: law enforcement facilities (without chief administrator's written consent)
detention facilities, prisons and jails
courtrooms (unless the judge permits)
portion of a bar/establishment primarily devoted to serving alcohol
K-12 school facilities for enrolled students
public K-12 and college facilities for anyone without a Wyoming-issued permit
state-operated or licensed health and human services residential facilities
facilities with explosive or volatile materials
the state hospital, Wyoming boys'/girls' schools and correctional facilities
places where federal or state law prohibits (e.g. airport sterile areas, Army Corps of Engineers property)

noGunSigns.notes: Posted signs count as trespass notice; remaining is criminal trespass (up to 6 months/$750).

openCarry.notes: Open carry legal at 18+; localities cannot ban it. Government entities may prohibit open carry in their facilities or campuses.

notes: Campus and K-12 carry is only for Wyoming-issued permit holders; visitors cannot carry there under permitless carry or out-of-state permits.
No carry in the bar portion of establishments serving alcohol.
Wyoming does not issue non-resident permits.
Permitless carry age lowered to 18 on 7/1/2026; some page notes still say 21.
Government entities may ban open carry in their facilities even where concealed carry is allowed.
